name: Ahiman
overview: Ahiman was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as one of the gatekeepers, a unique role that involved guarding the entrances to the sanctuary. His role is specifically noted in 1 Chronicles 9:17, highlighting his responsibility within the Levitical duties. There are no additional notes recorded about his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahiman means '[my] brother is a gift,' which reflects a personal or familial blessing. This proper name, as given in 1 Chronicles 9:17, was not directly assigned by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Ahiman is explicitly identified as a descendant of Korah, connecting him to a notable Levitical family line as stated in 1 Chronicles 9:19. Beyond this, Scripture does not record other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Ahiman's importance lies in his role as a gatekeeper within the tribe of Levi, entrusted with the sacred task of guarding the sanctuary. His connection to Korah places him within a significant Levitical lineage, emphasizing the continuity of priestly service. Through his service, Ahiman contributed to the orderly worship and protection of the holy place, reflecting God's provision for reverent access to His presence.
